merger_name: Google Australia – indefeasible rights to use terrestrial dark fibre from Telstra
merger_description:
Google Australia Pty Ltd (**Google Australia**) and Google Singapore Pte. Ltd. (**Google Singapore**) are indirect subsidiaries of Google LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, owned by Alphabet, Inc.

Telstra Singapore Pte. Ltd. (**Telstra Singapore**) and Telstra Corporation Limited (**Telstra Corporation**) are subsidiaries of Telstra Group Limited, a telecommunications and technology company with its primary operations in Australia.

The application concerns the acquisition of rights to use dark fibre pairs on Telstra’s Aura Network. The Aura Network is a terrestrial network of fibre optic cables. Fibre optic networks allow large volumes of data to be transmitted quickly and reliably over long distances.

Specifically, the Acquisition comprises:

* Google Australia acquiring from Telstra Corporation indefeasible rights to use (**IRUs**) certain dark fibre pairs on specified routes on Telstra’s terrestrial Aura Network, and associated colocation services, for a minimum term of 15 years, and
* Google Singapore acquiring from Telstra Singapore rights for Google Australia (or another affiliate) to acquire additional IRUs for dark fibre pairs on the Aura Network, and associated colocation services.

events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Google Australia Pty Ltd (Google Australia) and Google Singapore
Pte. Ltd. (Google Singapore) applied for a notification waiver in
respect of their proposed acquisition of indefeasible rights to use
(IRUs) certain dark fibre pairs from subsidiaries of Telstra Group
Limited, Telstra Singapore Pte. Ltd. (Telstra Singapore) and Telstra
Corporation Limited (Telstra Corporation), as described in the
transaction documents provided as part of the application (the
Acquisition).
The Acquisition involves:
• Google Australia acquiring from Telstra Corporation IRUs
certain dark fibre pairs on specified routes on Telstra’s
terrestrial Aura Network, and associated colocation services,
for a minimum term of 15 years; and
• Google Singapore acquiring from Telstra Singapore rights
for Google Australia (or another affiliate) to acquire
additional IRUs for dark fibre pairs on the Aura Network, and
associated colocation services.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

Google Australia and Google Singapore, are indirect subsidiaries of
Google LLC (together, Google Group), a Delaware limited liability
company owned by Alphabet, Inc.
Telstra Singapore Pte. Ltd. (Telstra Singapore) and Telstra
Corporation Limited (Telstra Corporation) are subsidiaries of Telstra
Group Limited (Telstra), a telecommunications and technology
company with its primary operations in Australia.
The Acquisition concerns rights to use dark fibre pairs on Telstra’s
Aura Network, a terrestrial network of fibre optic cables. Fibre optic
networks allow large volumes of data to be transmitted quickly and
reliably over long distances.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. post-Acquisition, Google Group’s share of fibre pairs
and/or capacity on each of the terrestrial cables the
subject of the Acquisition is expected to be small
b. there are alternative providers of terrestrial dark fibre and
capacity on terrestrial cables in Australia
c. the Acquisition is unlikely to foreclose access to the
remaining fibre pairs on the relevant terrestrial cables or to
capacity on alternative terrestrial cables in Australia for
Google Group’s downstream rivals.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
